title: Thomas precession
intro: In physics, the Thomas precession, named after Llewellyn Thomas, is a relativistic correction that applies to the spin of an elementary particle or the rotation of a macroscopic gyroscope. It relates the angular velocity of the spin of a particle following a curvilinear orbit to the angular velocity of the orbital motion.

title: Thompson order formula
intro: In mathematical finite group theory, the Thompson order formula, introduced by John Griggs Thompson (Held 1969, p.279), gives a formula for the order of a finite group in terms of the centralizers of involutions, extending the results of Brauer & Fowler (1955).

title: Three cups problem
intro:
The three cups problem, also known as the three cup challenge and other variants, is a mathematical puzzle that, in its most common form, cannot be solved.
In the beginning position of the problem, one cup is upside-down and the other two are right-side up.

title: Three subgroups lemma
intro: In mathematics, more specifically group theory, the three subgroups lemma is a result concerning commutators. It is a consequence of Philip Hall and Ernst Witt's eponymous identity.

title: Tietze extension theorem
intro: In topology, the Tietze extension theorem (also known as the Tietze–Urysohn–Brouwer extension theorem or Urysohn-Brouwer lemma) states that any real-valued, continuous function on a closed subset of a normal topological space can be extended to the entire space, preserving boundedness if necessary.

title: Time hierarchy theorem
intro: In computational complexity theory, the time hierarchy theorems are important statements about time-bounded computation on Turing machines. Informally, these theorems say that given more time, a Turing machine can solve more problems.

title: Tits alternative
intro: In mathematics, the Tits alternative, named after Jacques Tits, is an important theorem about the structure of finitely generated linear groups.

title: Titu's lemma
intro: In mathematics, Titu's lemma (also known as Bergström's inequality, Engel's form or Sedrakyan's inequality) is an algebraic inequality that establishes a lower bound for the sum of fractions whose numerators are squares of real numbers. It is a direct consequence of the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

title: Toda's theorem
intro: Toda's theorem is a result in computational complexity theory that was proven by Seinosuke Toda in his paper "PP is as Hard as the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy" and was given the 1998 Gödel Prize.
